title: Don't waste the day (Avot 3:10)
hookLine: Dosa ben Harkinas: late sleep, midday wine and idle company slowly waste a life
tomorrow: what costs more than money and takes one sentence?

cards: The alarm goes off, gets snoozed, gets snoozed again. Then it's noon, then a scroll that somehow lasts until the light changes. Where does a whole day go?

Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas lists the leaks in Avot: morning sleep, midday wine, children's chatter, and sitting in the gatherings of people who don't care to learn. These, he says, take a person out of the world.

teach.b: Today's question: where does a life actually go? Dosa's answer: not in one disaster. In small leaks.
None of the four is evil alone; a nap is not a sin. Together, they drift a person out of the world: out of the shared life of study, prayer and work.
Look at the first leak in Hebrew: sheinah shel shacharit, morning sleep. Shacharit is the morning prayer, from shachar, dawn. The hour that could have met the day slides by under a blanket.

A short chapter of the Qur'an, Al-Asr, opens in Pickthall's translation, "By the declining day," and says humanity is in a state of loss, except those who believe and do good works, and urge one another to truth and to endurance.

teach.h: TWO VOICES, ONE REFUSAL TO DRIFT.
teach.b: Shared ground: time leaks away, and the answer is found with other people, urging each other on, not alone.

An honest difference: Dosa names the leaks, in the setting of Torah and its community; Al-Asr names who is spared the loss, those who believe and do good and encourage each other, in the Qur'an's own covenant.
Two scriptures, each in its own voice, both refusing to let a day just drift.

how: Jews traditionally begin the day with Shacharit, the morning prayer, and some set a fixed time for study each day, a practice the Talmud calls setting times for Torah.

games.q: what does “don't waste the day” mean?
o: notice the small habits that quietly drain a life
never sleep after sunrise, even when you're ill
fill every hour so there's no time to rest

games.q: where the day goes — tap the pairs.

s: Dosa's 'morning sleep' uses the word for the morning prayer, Shacharit
sheinah shel shacharit: the sleep of the dawn hour.
Avot says one lazy morning ruins a life
it names habits that, together, slowly take a person out of the world.
a chapter of the Qur'an opens by swearing by the day's end

games.q: your brother sleeps until noon every weekend and says rest is holy too. what's the fair reading of Dosa's list?
o: rest isn't the problem; hours drifting away unnoticed are.
any sleep after sunrise is forbidden in Avot.
weekends don't count; Avot means workdays only.
games.why: Dosa names small habits that, together, take a person out of the world. rest has its place; the warning is the drift.

practice: Before you settle, stand and take a slow walk for a minute, around the room or down a hall, and with each few steps name one hour of yesterday and where it went. Then sit, and choose one hour of tomorrow to reclaim.
Give it a name before it arrives.

wordCard.voice: Don't waste the day: Dosa ben Harkinas's four small leaks, and the life they slowly draw out of the world.

orig.note: Hebrew: morning sleep, Avot 3:10; the same word as Shacharit, the morning prayer.

carryVoice: The line to carry: don't waste the day, one leak at a time. Sleep well, but not through the dawn.

sources.ref: Mishnah, Pirkei Avot 3:10 (Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas)
Qur'an 103:2–3 (Al-Asr: humanity in loss, except those who believe, do good works, and urge one another to truth and to endurance)
